app.name: FairSplit
app.tagline: Split group expenses fairly — at your own exchange rate.

landing.headline: Text it in. FairSplit settles it.
landing.subhead: Type an expense the way you'd text a friend — the rate, the receipt and who had what get sorted for you.

points.rate: The rate is fetched for you, and money from a travel card is counted at what you actually paid for it.
points.receipt: Photograph the receipt and the line items fill themselves in.
points.items: Tick who had what, quantity included. Nobody pays for a dish they never touched.

landing.caption: FairSplit is the treasurer of your group trip — text an expense in, Sem settles it.

letter.p1: Text me what you spent the way you would text a friend — "lunch 12000, Minsu and me" — and I settle it. No forms, no spreadsheet.
letter.p1Highlight: text me what you spent the way you would text a friend
letter.p2: The exchange rate is fetched for you, and money from a travel card is counted at what you actually paid for it. Photograph the receipt and the line items fill themselves in.
letter.p3: Tick who had what, quantity included. Nobody pays for a dish they never touched. When the trip ends, I hand everyone the shortest list of who pays whom.

rate.v: Fetched for you. Travel-card money counts at what you paid for it.

guide.title: How to use FairSplit
guide.intro: You record an expense in a few taps. A few more things worth knowing before you start.

why.rateTitle: It settles at what your money cost you
why.rateBody: Record what you paid to exchange money — ₩450,000 for ¥50,000 — and everything spent from that wallet settles at that rate. Today's market rate is fetched automatically when you need one instead.
why.receiptBody: Photograph it and the items come back as lines you can correct, rather than a total you have to break down by hand.
why.itemsBody: An expense can be split by who actually had each line, down to the quantity. Anything nobody claims is shared out.

steps.groupTitle: Join a group, or start one
steps.groupBody: An invite link puts you straight into your friend's group. Starting your own takes a name, the currency you will settle in, and where you are going.
steps.walletTitle: Add a wallet, then top it up
steps.walletBody: Exchanged cash, a travel card, a prepaid card — each one is a wallet. Add one from Wallets & top-ups in the menu, and recording a top-up is what teaches the app your own exchange rate.
steps.chatBody: Add manually from the menu walks you through it — amount, who paid, who is in. You can photograph the receipt there too and the items come back as lines.
steps.assignBody: Tick the people on each line, quantity included. Anything nobody ticks is shared between everyone on that expense.
steps.settleBody: Status, from the menu, shows what you fronted, what your own share came to, and what you are owed or owe with each person. Tap a name for the full history between the two of you.

guide.again: You can open this guide again any time from Account.

preview.what: FairSplit splits a trip's expenses — at the rate your money actually cost you.

exchange.title: Wallets & top-ups
exchange.walletQuestion: Which wallet did the money go into?
exchange.rateHint: The rate on your receipt or in the app you exchanged with.
exchange.paidComputed: Computed from the rate — edit it if you know the exact amount.
exchange.deleteConfirm: Delete this top-up? The balance and rate of {label} will change.
exchange.noRecords: Nothing loaded onto this wallet yet.

prompt.question: Exchanged cash or loaded a travel card for this trip? Log it once and we'll track the balance and your real rate.

wallet.title: Wallets
wallet.payAsYouGoNote: Converted by the bank at purchase time — today's market rate.
wallet.overdrawn: {amount} over — a top-up is probably missing
wallet.overdrawnHint: More was spent from this wallet than was ever loaded onto it — so either you topped it up and never logged it, or an expense only came out of here in part. Manage wallets works the top-up out from what is really on it; the other one is fixed on the expense.
wallet.noTopUps: No top-ups logged — market rate until you add one
wallet.adjustExplainer: If the app's balance doesn't match your real wallet, set it to the real amount.
wallet.countHelp: Type what is really on it. More than expected means a top-up you never logged, and we will ask what it cost; less means spending you never logged. Either way it changes this wallet, not what anyone owes.
wallet.countNothing: Matches the records — nothing to adjust.
wallet.countShortfall: {amount} less than the records explain — spending of your own that never got logged.
wallet.countSurplus: {amount} more than the records explain. Money only gets into this wallet one way, so you topped it up and never logged it. What did it cost?
wallet.topUpCostRequired: Say what the top-up cost — that price is this wallet's rate for every expense paid from it.
wallet.adjustmentRemoveConfirm: Remove this adjustment? The balance goes back to what the records say.
wallet.label: Name
wallet.deleteConfirm: Delete {label}? Its top-ups go with it. Only possible while nothing has been paid from it.
wallet.deleteBlocked: Expenses were paid from this wallet, so it stays.
wallet.none: No wallets yet. Add one for the cash or the travel card you're carrying.
wallet.tripPrompt: Heading to {place}? Log the cash you exchanged or the travel card you loaded, and every expense will convert at what your money actually cost.

loading.status: Sem is adding up who owes whom…

tips.0: Split by item when one of you skipped the wine.
tips.1: Log a cash exchange once and every cash expense uses your real rate.
tips.2: A travel card is a wallet — top it up and watch it drain.
tips.3: Tap a person to see only what the two of you shared.
tips.4: Photograph the receipt before the table clears it away.
tips.5: Enter the amount in the currency you actually paid.
tips.6: Someone else can add the expense they paid for.
tips.7: Cancelled an expense by mistake? Restore is one tap.
tips.8: Your share is what you ate. What you fronted is what you paid.
tips.10: Set the trip's country and the currency follows.
tips.11: The market rate is the bank's starting point, not its price.
tips.12: Correct a card expense once your statement posts.
tips.13: Nothing is settled until you settle it — these are estimates.
tips.14: Personal expenses stay yours and split with nobody.
tips.15: Rename yourself per group; other people see that name.
tips.16: Hide your wallet if the balance is nobody's business.
tips.17: A quantity of three, taken one each, is three shares.
tips.18: Untaken items are shared out, never dropped.
tips.19: Leaving a group keeps the history for everyone else.

explain.WALLET_AVG_COST: Converted at what the money in that wallet actually cost — the average of its logged top-ups.
explain.MARKET_SNAPSHOT: Converted at the market rate captured when the expense was entered.
explain.ACTUAL_CHARGED: Uses the amount the payer's bank actually billed.
explain.MARKET_FALLBACK: That wallet has no top-ups logged yet, so the market rate was used.
explain.OWN_EXCHANGE_RATE: Converted at the rate you told us you exchanged at — money you prepaid but keep no wallet for.
explain.SPLIT_FUNDING: Paid from more than one source. Each part was converted at its own rate, so no single rate covers the whole amount.

form.personal: Personal expense (not settled with the group)
form.actualChargedNote: If you know the exact figure your bank billed, it beats any rate we could look up.
form.refundHint: Refund — negative amount, money coming back.
form.itemsOptional: Items are optional. Skip this and the total splits evenly between everyone sharing.
form.unassignedNotice: Unassigned lines are split in proportion to what each person had.
form.assignSplitByAmount: {quantity} doesn't divide by {count}, so this line is split equally by amount.
form.noItemsToAssign: No items to assign — the total splits evenly between everyone sharing.
form.assignOver: That is {assigned} units of {quantity} — more than this line has. Fix it before saving.
form.assignPartial: {remaining} unit(s) left over — their value is split in proportion to what each person had.
form.discrepancy: Items add up to {items} but the receipt says {receipt} — a difference of {amount}. The difference is still shared out; nothing is dropped.
form.rateBasis: Market rate. Your bank or card will charge a little more.
form.rateUnavailableInline: No live rate for {currency} — enter it manually on the next step.
form.manualHint: This is the MARKET rate for the day — not your own wallet's rate.
form.rateUnusual: This rate looks unusual — the market rate is {unit} {currency} = {rate} {settlement}.
form.paidFromQuestion: Was this prepaid money, or paid on the spot?
form.prepaidOptionNote: Cash or a travel card you topped up before spending it.
form.onTheSpotOptionNote: A card, or cash you changed at a booth and spent straight away. Converts at the market rate.
form.whichWallet: Which one did it come out of?
form.noWalletsYet: You have no wallets set up. Just tell us the rate you got — we can save it as a wallet afterwards if you want.
form.ownRateHint: The rate YOU exchanged at — not today’s market rate.
form.shortfallQuestion: {amount} is still missing. How did you cover it?
form.answerTill: I topped it up on the spot
form.answerTillNote: Exchanged more at the counter and put it on {label}.
form.answerOnTheSpot: I paid the rest on the spot
form.answerOnTheSpotNote: A card, or cash changed and spent straight away.
form.portionTitle: Part of it came from somewhere else
form.tillDialogNote: This is saved as a top-up of that wallet, dated to the expense.
form.answerSomeoneElseNote: They fronted part of this receipt, so the group owes them for it.
form.splitAdd: Some of it came from somewhere else
form.splitOver: That is {amount} more than the expense.
form.tillAmountLabel: How much you put on it ({currency})
form.reviewSplitTitle: Paid from more than one source
form.paidFromHint: Prepaid money converts at what that wallet cost you. A pay-as-you-go card converts at the market rate.
form.newCashWalletNote: We will start a cash wallet for {currency} when you save.
form.topUpQuestion: Exchanged more, or loaded your card?
form.addWalletLink: Add a travel card or another wallet
form.otherCurrencyWallet: You have {count, plural, one {a {currency} wallet} other {# {currency} wallets}}: {wallets}.
form.noteMarketMode: This group settles at the market rate, whatever it was paid with.
form.splitAgreesRounded: Rows add up to {sum} — {diff} more than the {total} total, because each share rounds up so the payer is never left short.
form.derivationRounding: Rounded up to the next whole {settlement} so the payer is never left short.
form.derivationSame: Same currency as the group, so no conversion.
form.derivationSplit: Converted part by part, each at the rate of whichever source paid it — so no single rate covers the whole receipt.

scan.name: Item name
scan.taxIncluded: Tax is included in the item prices

scan.totalOnlyNotice: The items couldn't be read — using just the printed total.

scan.tooLarge: That photo is too large. Try a smaller one, or type the expense in.

wallet.needCurrency: Pick which currency this wallet holds.

batch.title: Review before saving
batch.summary: {rows, plural, one {# line read} other {# lines read}}. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
batch.checksumMismatch: Total line says {declared}, but the rows add up to {sum}.
batch.checksumExcluded: {count, plural, one {# row in another currency is not counted} other {# rows in another currency are not counted}}.
batch.confirm: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing ready to save} one {Save 1 row} other {Save # rows}}
batch.skipped: {count, plural, one {# row is left open} other {# rows are left open}} — nothing is discarded.
batch.checksumUnreadable: The total line's amount could not be read, so nothing is compared against it.
batch.checksumUnparsable: {count, plural, one {# row's amount could not be read} other {# rows' amounts could not be read}}.
batch.checksumNotAllReady: {count, plural, one {# of the rows it adds up is still open} other {# of the rows it adds up are still open}}.
batch.mergeBlocked: Cannot merge: there is no boundary between this row and the next.
batch.scopeRevoked: Revoked — this line no longer applies across rows.

unreadReason.unparsed: An amount was found but no expense could be read around it.
unreadReason.cross-row-reference: Refers to another line, so it cannot be read alone.
unreadReason.residual-arithmetic: States a remainder, not an amount of its own.

home.estimates: Estimates — final numbers at checkpoint settlement.
home.breakdownSplitRate: Each part at its own rate
home.summaryNote: Fronted minus your share roughly explains the sum of the amounts above — rounding always favours whoever paid, so the gap can grow a little with every unevenly split expense you fronted.
home.feedNote: Amounts are your share, not the receipt total.
home.feedNone: Nothing of yours on this one.
